subject: Vanguard Systems - Integration adoption playbook & rollout Q&A
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@vanguard.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@vanguard.com>, IT Ops <it_ops@vanguard.com>

Subject: RFP follow-up: migration & roll-out details needed

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our RFP scoring we need a consolidated response to the implementation and migration section (Appendix C). Specifically we need:
- A week-by-week migration timeline for a 3-phase rollout (pilot -> phased rollout -> production) including estimated downtime windows and cutover steps.
- Canary strategy description and rollback criteria.
- Integration touchpoints (SSO, SCIM, logging/export, network egress rules).
- Evidence of audit/logging capabilities and retained fields for compliance (SOC2 scope).

I've attached the Appendix C spreadsheet with our fields — please return a populated copy and any supporting runbooks by EOD Friday. Also flag anything that requires legal/ps procurement involvement.

Elena

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: migration & roll-out details needed

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and for sending Appendix C. Attaching our initial responses and a short playbook for your review. High-level summary below; full details are in the attached spreadsheet and runbook.

1) Proposed timeline (8 weeks total):
   - Week 1-2: Onboarding & environment prep (VPC peering, firewall rules, SSO/SAML test)
   - Week 3: Pilot — small user cohort (1-2 model endpoints, internal traffic only)
   - Week 4-5: Phased rollout — incremental traffic shifts (10% -> 50%) with monitoring gates
   - Week 6-7: Capacity scaling & latency validation under production-like load
   - Week 8: Final cutover & verification; runbook sign-off

   Downtime windows: rolling switch at the application layer; anticipated <5 minutes for model swap with session-preserving redirects.

2) Canary strategy & rollback criteria:
   - Canary runs for a minimum of 48h on real traffic mirrored at 10% with canary-specific metrics (latency p95, error-rate, model-output pass rate vs. golden prompts).
   - Automatic rollback triggers: p95 latency > 2x baseline for >15m, error-rate >1% for >10m, quality regression detected on key prompt-set (configurable).
   - Manual abort: Ops can abort via console; automated fallback to last-stable model variant is available.

3) Integration touchpoints:
   - SSO: SAML 2.0 + optional OIDC hooks, SCIM for user provisioning
   - Logging: token-level and request-level traces retained for 90 days by default; configurable retention for compliance
   - Network: VPC peering and egress IP allowlist; private endpoints available for Private deployments

4) Evidence & artifacts: attached runbook, canary playbook (pdf), and a populated Appendix C sheet.

Notes: A couple of Appendix fields (audit-export schema and retention SLA exceptions) will need security sign-off — looping Marissa for details.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: migration & roll-out details needed

Elena — looping in answers inline and attaching the detailed rollback checklist and export SLA.

On Tue, Sep 16, 2026 at 10:22 AM Elena Morales <elena.morales@vanguard.com> wrote:
> - For the 48h canary, do you mirror traffic or reroute a sampled portion?

We support both modes. Recommendation for Vanguard: mirrored traffic into a canary cluster for read-only verification (no downstream commit) for first 24h, then a sampled 10% live routing for functional verification. Mirroring minimizes downstream exposure while giving realistic request shapes.

> - For rollback, can you provide an exact list of checks your automation runs before initiating an auto-rollback (we have to map these to our incident runbooks)?

Auto-rollback checks (automated agent runs every 60s):
  * p95 latency cross-check vs baseline (threshold configurable)
  * 502/5xx spike detection (absolute and relative thresholds)
  * Output-validation scores on configured golden prompt-set (lower-bound threshold)
  * Memory/KV-cache pressure above safe threshold (host-level)
  * Model-serving instance health (process crashes or OOM)

If any of the above persist for configured windows (default 10–15m), we mark as automated rollback. All checks and thresholds can be tuned on the rollout policy.

> - Audit logs: can you export the raw request logs (anonymized) for our SOC team on-demand? What is the SLA for export?

Yes — raw request logs can be exported with field-level anonymization options. Standard SLA for ad-hoc exports is 3 business days; expedited 1 business day is available as part of an enterprise support add-on. Logs are delivered to a customer-owned S3 bucket or secure SCP endpoint.

> - Does the Private deployment option support HSM-backed keys for customer-managed encryption?

Yes — Private supports KMS integrations and HSM (Bring-Your-Own-HSM) for key material; we can document the integration touchpoints.

> Procurement: migration credits/discounts during pilot?

We typically offer a pilot credit package (negotiable) that covers baseline inference consumption for the pilot period. I'll have Commercial loop in if you want a concrete proposal.

Attaching: redeploy_rollback_checklist.docx and export_sla_matrix.pdf.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
